tools.name: smile_list_customers
tools.description: List loyalty-program customers, newest first, with their points balance, state and VIP tier id. Look a customer up by exact email, or filter by state or last-updated time. Cursor-paginated (metadata.next_cursor). Smile: GET /customers.

tools.name: smile_get_customer
tools.description: Fetch one customer by Smile customer ID: name, email, state, points_balance, referral_url, vip_tier_id, and optionally their VIP status with current and next tier. Smile: GET /customers/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_points_transactions
tools.description: List points transactions (every earn, spend and manual adjustment), newest first — e.g. a customer's full points history. Each has points_change (+/-), a customer-visible description and a merchant internal_note. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /points_transactions.

tools.name: smile_get_points_transaction
tools.description: Fetch one points transaction by ID. Smile: GET /points_transactions/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_points_products
tools.description: List points products — the rewards customers can buy with points. 'fixed' products cost points_price; 'variable' products trade variable_points_step points for variable_points_step_reward_value, between variable_points_min and variable_points_max. Each embeds its reward. Page-numbered (page, page_si

tools.name: smile_get_points_product
tools.description: Fetch one points product (a way to redeem points) by ID, including its reward. Smile: GET /points_products/{id}.

tools.name: smile_list_reward_fulfillments
tools.description: List rewards that have been issued to customers — usually discount codes — with code, fulfillment_status (pending/issued/cancelled/failed), usage_status (used/unused/untracked), used_at and expires_at. Use customer_id to answer 'what codes does this customer have?'. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /rew

tools.name: smile_list_earning_rules
tools.description: List the enabled earning rules — the ways customers earn points or rewards (placing an order, signing up, birthdays, custom activities), with reward, reward_value, earning_limit and any VIP-tier restriction. Cursor-paginated. Smile: GET /earning_rules.

tools.name: smile_list_vip_tiers
tools.description: List the VIP program's tiers, sorted by milestone (the threshold to reach each tier), optionally with each tier's perks and entry rewards. Smile: GET /vip_tiers.

tools.name: smile_get_points_settings
tools.description: Fetch the points program's configuration, e.g. the points currency label ("Points", "Stars"). Smile: GET /points_settings.

tools.name: smile_get_referral_settings
tools.description: Fetch the referral program's configuration: whether it is active, and the sender (advocate) and receiver (friend) rewards. Smile: GET /referral_settings.

tools.name: smile_create_points_transaction
tools.description: WRITE: add or deduct points from a customer's balance (a manual adjustment, e.g. a goodwill credit or a correction). points_change > 0 adds, < 0 deducts; Smile rejects a deduction that would make the balance negative. Undo by creating an opposite adjustment. `description` is shown to the customer; `

tools.name: smile_create_activity
tools.description: WRITE: record that a customer performed an action (identified by an activity type token configured in Smile Admin, e.g. a custom 'newsletter signup' activity). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: smile_list_customers, smile_get_customer · Private data: smile_create_activity · Public sink: smile_list_customers, smile_get_customer, smile_create_points_transaction, smile_create_activity, smile_purchase_points_product.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: smile_list_customers, smile_get_customer · Private data: smile_create_activity · Public sink: smile_list_customers, smile_get_customer, smile_create_points_transaction, smile_create_activity, smile_purchase_points_product

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
